title: Protocol for Assessing Distances in Pathway Space for Classifier Feature Sets
author: Tercan, Apolonio, et al.
materials: In this step, we download and install R and RStudio, followed by the PathwaySpace package.1.Download and install R and RStudio.a.To download R: https://cran.r-project.org/b.To download RStudio: https://rstudio.com/products/rstudio/2.Download and install PathwaySpace in RStudio:> install.packages("PathwaySpace")Note: Additional R dependencies will be automatically downloaded during installation, including RGraphSpace, igraph, ggplot2, ggrepel, RANN, and scales packages.
No materials were generated in this study.

steps.title: Prepare computational environment
steps.instruction: Ensure the computer has at least 16 GB RAM. Install R (version ≥ 4.4) from https://cran.r-project.org and RStudio (v.2023.06.1) from https://posit.co/products/open-source/rstudio/. Then install the PathwaySpace package (v.1.0.0) in RStudio; all required dependencies (RGraphSpace, igraph, ggplot2, ggrepel, RANN, scales) will be installed automatically.

steps.title: Load packages and Pathway Commons graph
steps.instruction: Load the necessary R libraries, import the pre‑processed Pathway Commons v12 igraph object, verify its size, identify top‑connected hub genes, and display the graph layout with hub annotations.

substeps.instruction: Identify the top‑10 hub genes (highest degree centrality) and store in `top10hubs` (e.g., "GNB1", "TRIM28", "RPS27A", "CTNNB1", "TP53", "ACTB").
Plot the graph layout with hub genes highlighted in blue: `plotGraphSpace(PCv12_pruned_igraph, marks = top10hubs, mark.color = "blue")`.

steps.title: Build PathwaySpace object and create gene lists
steps.instruction: Construct a PathwaySpace object from the loaded graph, load the Hallmark P53 gene set, intersect it with the graph, and generate two random 50‑gene lists (L1 and L2) with reproducible seeds; then assess their overlap with a hypergeometric test and note alternative flat‑file loading.

substeps.instruction: Extract the P53 Hallmark pathway: `HALLMARK_P53_PATHWAY <- Hallmarks_v2023_1_Hs_symbols$HALLMARK_P53_PATHWAY` and confirm its length: `length(HALLMARK_P53_PATHWAY)  # → 173`.
Intersect the Hallmark set with the PathwaySpace object (implicit in subsequent steps).
- Set seed 12 and sample 50 genes: `set.seed(12); L1 <- sample(HALLMARK_P53_PATHWAY, 50)`.
- Set seed 34 and sample another 50 genes: `set.seed(34); L2 <- sample(HALLMARK_P53_PATHWAY, 50)`.
Perform a one‑sided hypergeometric test: `phyper(q = 11, m = 50, n = 173-50, k = 50, lower.tail = FALSE)  # → 0.86` (p‑value).

Optional: download the provided CSV file (DataS1) and load with `GeneList <- read.csv("path/to/file.csv")`; then verify membership with `all(L1 %in% names(pspace_PCv12))` and `all(L2 %in% names(pspace_PCv12))` (both return TRUE).

steps.title: Visualize gene‑list densities in pathway space
steps.instruction: Assign a signal of 1 to the genes in each list (0 to all others) and generate density plots for L1 and L2 within the PathwaySpace object.

substeps.instruction: Set signal for L1: `vertexSignal(pspace_PCv12)[L1] <- 1` (all other vertices remain 0).
Plot L1 density: `plotPathwaySpace(pspace_PCv12, marks = "TP53", mark.size = 2, theme = "th3", title = "Density of L1 genes in PathwaySpace")`.
Plot L2 density: `plotPathwaySpace(pspace_PCv12, marks = "TP53", mark.size = 2, theme = "th3", title = "Density of L2 genes in PathwaySpace")`.

steps.title: Compute and plot pathway‑space distances
steps.instruction: Calculate a vertex‑wise distance matrix for the graph, use the pathDistances() function to obtain the distance between L1 and L2 and between 10 000 random gene lists of equal size, and visualise the null distribution with the observed distance.

substeps.instruction: Compute the vertex‑wise distance matrix: `gdist <- vertexDist(pspace_PCv12)` (or the appropriate function name).
Calculate distances: `pdist <- pathDistances(pspace_PCv12, geneLists = list(L1, L2), nRandom = 10000)`.
